narrative: Material PL1__MC7A8839 exhibits variable demand with CV=0.827 and unstable lead times (CV=0.653, range 0.11–3.37 days). The current SAP policy (MOQ=SS=43) generates ~234 orders per year, creating unnecessary transaction costs. The optimized EOQ-based (r,Q) policy recommends order quantity 266 and safety stock 78 to maintain a 95% service level, reducing total annual inventory cost by $7,724 (61.2%). Storage capacity is not binding. Safety lead time in SAP can be reduced from 2.0 to 1.26 days.

research_insights.selected_model: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) with (r,Q) continuous-review policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: EOQ is appropriate given continuous demand (79.1% non-zero days), sufficient history (220 observations), and the need to balance ordering vs. holding costs. The combined-variance safety stock formula accounts for both demand variability (CV=0.827) and lead time instability (CV=0.653). Continuous review (r,Q) is preferred over periodic review due to high demand variability and the cost of stockouts.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Lead time instability (CV=0.653) is the dominant risk: if lead times spike above 3.37 days (observed max), the safety stock of 78 units may be insufficient. Storage capacity (1,366.5 units) is not currently binding (SS+OQ=344), but leaves ample headroom. Demand variability should be monitored quarterly and safety stock recalculated if CV changes materially.
